reviews.text: Takes the superhero format and sucks the life from it, reducing the usual expansive Marvel feast to the thinnest of gruel.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: In the age of multiverses and reality alterations, simplicity has never looked so bright.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: It's a horrific mish-mash of other films that ends with two CGI monsters punching each other into walls while screaming about “ultimate power”.
reviews.author: Paul Klein

reviews.text: The best part of “Morbius” were the opening and closing credits. It had a James Turrell color aesthetic with a dash of Nicholas Winding Refn’s “The Neon Demon” (2016).
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: After multiple delays, Morbius, the “highly anticipated” new entry into Sony’s Spider-Man Universe, arrives with some of the worst world-building we have seen in a long time.
reviews.author: Hector A. Gonzalez

reviews.text: Morbius is a thin piece that lacks any reason to entice comic book fans, genre fans, or action fans.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: I can't even comprehend how they thought this was worth putting out. Worst of all, it connects itself to an actual good Spider-Man villain.
reviews.author: Cris Parker

reviews.text: A terribly dull movie that takes you back to the worst CBM’s in the 2000s. Jared Leto brings dedication, Matt Smith brings charm & is having the time of his life…. But god the script, the editing, the pacing was all terribly brought together
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: It’s not that Morbius is bad, but that it is so bad that it’s almost unwatchable. Matt Smith is a waste of great talent in a role that sees him go from practically paralyzed to supervillain in a matter of seconds.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: From the predictability and zero creativity of the main plot to the heavy reliance on uninteresting, unnecessary exposition, Daniel Espinosa finds his most significant problem in the blatant lack of care in the treatment of the characters.
reviews.author: Manuel São Bento

reviews.text: It comes as no surprise that the extremely delayed Moribus is not the finest superhero movie ever released. The film lacks depth and intrigue. It’s a slow-moving exploration of a character that barely makes the case for its existence.
reviews.author: Tina Kakadelis

reviews.text: Rumours circulating about Morbius made me apprehensive about attending the press screening, to begin with. But I went into it hoping for better. Unfortunately, the movie ended up being even worse than the rumours led me to believe.
reviews.author: M.X. Katyayani

reviews.text: In the end, there’s a reason why Gen Z decided that the funniest thing they could say about it was that it was good, with their almost supernatural grasp of irony they can see that of all the things this movie is, good is not even remotely one of them.
reviews.author: Sean Fallon

reviews.text: Sony Pictures has proved one thing: Morbius succeeds as a vampire film as it drains life from itself.
reviews.author: Annie Banks

reviews.text: Honestly, this is probably almost as good a Morbius film as you're going to get where it has a PG-13 rating and no Spider-Man involvement. Changing either of those things would have made it better.
reviews.author: Joseph Garcia

reviews.text: Morbius is neither as dire as you have heard nor is it incredibly good. It’s mid-tier Marvel, not particularly inspired but not the worst thing I’ve ever sat through. If anything, it kind of reminds me of the Underworld series.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: It’s a throwback in form, but not in personality. There’s nothing weird or dated about this movie; it’s just filling a superhero quota.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: The movie is only bland and unpersuasive, and would have disappeared without a trace if not for the jolly internet memes that snarkily celebrated it, as though it were a lovably inept thing to be cherished, not chastised, for its flaws.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Leto is certainly up for the role, and I can see where he could have done something special with a better script and more focused direction.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: The enjoyment of the film is certainly lessened by the film's darkness, and I don't mean its tonality.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: Even if you take the poor quality and bland performance from Leto out of consideration - Morbius barely feels like a movie.
reviews.author: Amanda the Jedi

reviews.text: There are no interesting characters, no clearly defined rules or powers, no exciting action setpieces, no eye-widening visual spectacle, and none of the sense of danger, addiction, or damnation you might assume would give something like this a spark.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: Falls apart at the halfway point due to its weak, and at times, laughable script and Jared Leto's lack of star power. It does, however, have a certain 'B' movie appeal.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: This misfire only sinks its teeth into bland monotony; vampires aren't the only things that suck within its frames.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Morbius fails to grab the audience from the beginning and a plot that has quite a bit of potential, simply put, falls flat.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: ... full of the kind of fantastical hijinks that make "Venom" (2018) and "Venom: Let There Be Carnage" (2021) popcorn delights, except where the nonsense in those films felt like part of the charm, here it’s an utter drag.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Sadly just about every element of the film ends up dragging it down, including a screenplay in search of a more compelling plot, a multitude of bland characters, cheap-looking special effects, and a very subdued lead performance from Jared Leto.
reviews.author: Jeff Beck

reviews.text: In the end, 'Morbius' feels like a rush to cash in on the strides the studio made with its more impressive features.
reviews.author: Murjani Rawls

reviews.text: ...feels like a generic template that someone forgot to fill in with interesting details before presenting it to the public.
reviews.author: Steve Biodrowski

reviews.text: I was feeling quite bored...They could have had a lot more fun with it.
reviews.author: Achara Kirk

reviews.text: It's very predictable…very melodramatic.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: A product that's empty, stunted, schizophrenic, induces the kind of tachycardia bad coffee can produce... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Morbius suffers from a case of the doldrums, and with very few opportunities for the cast to liven up the material, the movie simply languishes towards an unappealing ending.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: A multi-referential gazpacho... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: While it is a bit ridiculous and humble in its intentions, the film offers something to have fun with. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: A vampire movie, without too much blood or gore, but canonical. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fausto Fernandez

reviews.text:
Feels banal.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Pure formula… sustained with a special effects display that isn’t convincing or spectacular. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Daniel Espinosa's film isn't awful by definition, but it's another reminder that when a comic book adaptation is produced poorly and without a real identity, the stink is much worse when you leave the theater.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text:
Vacant, lacking purpose, and no clear objective.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aldo Javier Martínez

reviews.text:
A failed experiment from Marvel that resembles something akin to Count Dracula's second cousin. 
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Martínez

reviews.text: Lifeless...
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: Daniel Espinosa and his crew capably provide a rough and grungy Manhattan for Michael Morbius to hunt in. Morbius is a remarkable monster movie, powered by the brotherly love experienced by Michael and Lucian/Milo.
reviews.author: Benjamin Franz

reviews.text: With THE LITTLE THINGS and his sensational, transformation in HOUSE OF GUCCI, Leto is totally invested and gives the Marvel Universe a mesmerizing character shaped with conflicting appetites.
reviews.author: Victoria Alexander

reviews.text: ...a hit-and-miss adaptation that is, to an increasingly distressing extent, more miss than hit...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: While the initial cat-and-mouse chase is exciting, particularly as the super-humans face-off against each other, it does lose its momentum relatively quickly.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: It feels like there was a really decent draft of this movie waiting to be discovered, and, whilst it succeeds at times, instead, Morbius feels hollow and very much like a missed opportunity.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Despite Jared Leto being in this misbegotten affair, I have to say it did not rise to my expectations for it.
reviews.author: Lael Loewenstein

reviews.text: It doesn't do anything we haven't seen before. The visual effects are rather tired.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Odd that playing a man transforming into a vampire feels like a more lived-in, relaxed performance for Leto than his cartoonish Italian fop in "House of Gucci," but at least he seems to be having fun with it.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: If you want the scientific structure and creativity of Birdemic, this one's for you.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Playing the Living Vampire, Leto gets the benefit of introducing a Spider-man villain thats never been seen in live-action before. Unfortunately, his performance and most of Morbius as a whole are layered in melodrama and CGI fakery.
reviews.author: Drew Tinnin

reviews.text: A lot of this movie made zero sense. Trying to take elements from "No Way Home" and insert them in here was very misguided. This is an incredibly bad comic book film that revolves around one of the least interesting Spiderman villains.
reviews.author: Justin Brown

reviews.text: This was remarkably bad and somehow bored me to tears despite the insanity on-screen. The plot had more holes than swiss cheese. The character development was nonexistent. Please keep the MCU far, far away from what Sony is doing...
reviews.author: Brandon Collins

reviews.text: Somehow, Jared Leto is not even the best Jared in Morbius. Oh, I just, enough with the origin stories we did not ask for.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Simply put, Morbius is one of the laziest, shallowest, most pathetic attempts at a movie blockbuster in some time.
reviews.author: Jon Winkler

reviews.text: Not the epic disaster we expected...It is, however, generic as all hell.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: A case of (the filmmakers) had a character, but didnt quite know what to do with it. I think its quite a messy plot that doesnt always make that much sense A bit different with the horror theme, but nothing special.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The effects-laden film with its hollow storyline ends up being filler between web-slinger releases and it makes sure you know that thanks to all the SSU references.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Superficial character development, and shady morals, means it is hard to work up much sympathy for most of the characters in this movie, including Morbius himself. Who are we intended to identify with? Who are we intended to respect or admire?
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: This is what we've been waiting for since 2020? Yall are proud of this? Must be some type of happy accident for Sony to finally release this on April 1st because this movie's existence is a joke.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: 'Morbius' gives audiences little to sink their teeth into.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: An attempt to toss in some comedy fails miserably. The evil doings and essential fight come across as labored and expected for the genre.
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Will ‘Morbius’ go down as one of the worst Marvel-adjacent movies ever? That’s easy: Yes. But most of our Morbius questions are harder to answer.
reviews.author: Daniel Chin

reviews.text: If it were just a ride in a theme park, Morbius would be fun enough. But it is not.
reviews.author: Catey Sullivan

reviews.text: Maybe the sequel will be better because all the introductory stuff is stuffed into this sluggish overstuffed adventure movie. Besides I thought "Batman" owned the rights to the use of bats.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Morbius, at best, will be remembered as the latest effort on Sony's part to make its nascent Sinister Six franchise happen. And, like "fetch," it's hard to see that happening.
reviews.author: Liz Shannon Miller

reviews.text: Coming off the heels of superhero masterpieces such as Spider-Man: No Way Home and The Batman, Morbius is a movie you might stumble across on cable TV and play in the background as you do your household chores rather than appointment viewing.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: This is nothing less than an absolute fiasco, a dingy, instantly forgettable entry in the bargain-bin branch of the MCU that should be shoved back into its crypt and buried under an avalanche of bat guano.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Morbius becomes pat and predictable, with so-so FX that look like something from an “Underworld” flick from two decades ago.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Is it a movie you should see? Honestly, yes.
reviews.author: Andre Meadows

reviews.text: These kinds of movies are supposed to be morality tales in which the protagonist comes to a tragic end. But a tragic end cant become a franchise, so Morbius flinches from its necessary conclusion, leaving an already confused movie without a payoff.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: Doesn't deliver a lot of high notes, but it's not unwatchable (especially if you enjoy the vampire genre). "Morbius" is not as great as you'd hoped, but not as bad as you feared.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: There’s such little meat on the bone here plot-wise that it feels like everyone involved in the production got a checklist of beats that the studio wanted to hit and did their best to make that all that they did.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: Overall, this is an entertaining movie. It sucks you in with the action and standout scenes between some of the characters. But, while Morbius has the makings of a great anti-hero revival, it wavers with the execution.
reviews.author: Olivia Gacka

reviews.text: Sadly, director Daniel Espinosa's action horror is itself drained of atmosphere, shocks and drama.
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: Like the Venom films  and unlike the MCU movies  Morbius eschews the mythmaking of the Avengers for darkly comic horror.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: Morbius is an incoherent and unoriginal film that doesn’t make the best use of Jared Leto’s talents.
reviews.author: Emmanuel Noisette

reviews.text: Jared Leto has been exquisitely vulnerable (Requiem for a Dream), exquisitely sinister (Blade Runner 2049) and exquisitely ridiculous (House of Gucci). Yet in Morbius, he’s something he’s never been before: disastrously dull.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: A mishmash of shoddy-looking effects work and oddball creative choices, a mélange of nonsense that could have been somewhat forgiven if the movie was any fun ... but it isn't. In short, Morbius kind of sucks.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: So many choices... just seem halfhearted. They're not terrible, but they're also not interesting.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: I'd gone into Morbius expecting a throwaway comicbook movie, but the director Daniel Espinosa and writers Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless seem to have higher aspirations.
reviews.author: Peter Hoskin

reviews.text: It is dull and generic which is a real shame because the cast is talented and the premise has potential to be weird and exciting. In the end, its just forgettable.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The further I get from it, the more its flaws seem crippling, but I admire the spirit that Espinosa and company brought to the project, which, Im convinced, was nearly destroyed by a meddlesome and cowardly studio.
reviews.author: Ian Simmons

reviews.text: Morbius sometimes works great, but these memorable moments are spaced too sporadically throughout the film. It's worth watching to see the delightful performance from Matt Smith, who perfectly balances the campiest moments with the most emotional.
reviews.author: Amanda Mazzillo

reviews.text: Its hard to say if Morbius was doomed from the start, but after years of anticipating its tepid arrival, the final film earns a yawn as large as its protagonists unhinged snarl.
reviews.author: Brad Gullickson

reviews.text: Its unfair, but mostly accurate, to call Morbius a speed bump in the trajectory of comic book films.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: Ghoulish Gothic gloom....
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Here's Jared Leto, ditched from the DC Extended Universe for his hammy take on The Joker, starring in his first solo movie for Marvel. It's the dullest film to ever carry that flickering logo.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Just plain miserable to sit through, offering almost nothing pleasurable either ironically or unironically.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: ... we know where its been, where its going, and theres zero emotional impact when we get there without a hint of a denouement... a total DC-MurderVerse move to computer-animate the entire final battle climax...
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: An often bored-looking Leto isnt helped by a formulaic, generic, cliché-ridden screenplay credited to Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless. Anonymous, borderline competent direction comes thanks to Swedish-born Daniel Espinosas (Life, Safe House) ...
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: Ultimately I’ll say that the movie wasn’t the trainwreck I was expecting... But I’d rather see a flaming disaster from a team of passionate creatives than a sanitized jigsaw puzzle assembled by a board of directors any day.
reviews.author: Tori Preston

reviews.text: Like most April Fools' Day jokes, Morbius is not actually funny. It’s not bad in the ha ha you have to see this it’s so ridiculous kind of way. It just feels underbaked and lame -- and, sadly, not weird enough to be any kind of fun.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: As comic book movies go it's overwhelmingly underwhelming, a lifeless carcass of a film that serves its immediate purpose but inspires zero desire to have this character's story continue in future films.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Alas, the total quantity of wit in this movie is to a soupçon what Jared Leto is to Daniel Day-Lewis.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Morbius ultimately feels less than the sum of its parts. While there might have been a good movie somewhere pre-reshoots, the film never finds its footing. That said, it's not nearly as bad as others pre-decided it would be.
reviews.author: Sheraz Farooqi

reviews.text: Morbius is dreadful, quite possibly the worst example of the comic-book, super-hero genre I’ve ever seen.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: [An] incoherent, vampire-themed Marvel offcut.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Leto is smoothly charismatic but is given nothing of interest to do.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: A blood-sucking example of why not everything ever published by Marvel Comics deserves a movie.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Despite only being a little over 90 minutes long, Morbius is a chore to sit through. It lacks imagination, zest, and a thrill of discovery.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Morbius is a surprisingly solid building block for Sony as it looks to expand its universe of heroes and villains.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Morbius internal conflict is brushed aside and the movies central theme is abandoned and forgotten in a chaotic mass of special effects and a mad rush to set up more sequels.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: Take the legacy character out of the equation, and this is virtually indistinguishable from any garden-variety horrorthriller released in the post-Oscars dumping ground.
reviews.author: Martin Tsai

reviews.text: Finally, a full year after its initial release date, it is finally seeing the light of day. And let me be the one to say: I could have happily waited another decade.
reviews.author: Emma Kiely

reviews.text: Between the lack of atmosphere, underdeveloped characters and questionable visuals, Morbius just doesnt know how to hold its audiences attention.
reviews.author: James Hanton

reviews.text: Jared Leto trades in his clown shoes for fangs  and, of course, its as silly and bad as you thought. However, its never not entertaining, and Matt Smith understood the assignment.
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: Occasionally, it's not as ghastly as it might sound, mostly thanks to Leto's general gravitas and a supervillain (Matt Smith from "The Crown") thoroughly enjoying his own personal discoveries.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Its a bit like a hastily and inexpertly assembled jigsaw puzzle. While the overall picture is obvious, the individual pieces dont fit into place, and after awhile, you stop caring.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The misfiring "Morbius" at a certain point just stops firing, but not before it stops making sense.
reviews.author: André Hereford

reviews.text: ...despite aspirations to Cronenbergian body-horror, Morbius' bloody action amounts to a lengthy thin-off between Leto and Smith...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Although Dracula has long represented the outsider, Morbius spends the whole film trying to be more normal.
reviews.author: Noah Berlatsky

reviews.text: More horror than hero, Morbius is as dark and brooding as The Batman, but with less style and substance. Yet, the themes and origin story are intriguing, and a different product than routine Marvel comic books-turned-movies.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: A painfully boring, listless, tedious (slightly ableist) horror action film that never quite knows where it wants to go...
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: In short, going for the vampiric pun youd expect, this sucks.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: An interesting choice: Every fight sequence or use of superpowers in Morbius is done under a fart cloud. Some may say its vampire mist or puff of smoke, but I know a plume of flatulence when I see it.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: A mediocre mixed bag of a 90s B movie that, despite its many flaws, represents an acceptable introduction to Jared Leto's anti-hero.
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: At this point, I think it's fair to say that any comic book character that has even the most remote stink of Spider-Man on them is fair game for a film adaptation (I'm looking at you, Venom movies), whether they deserve one or not.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Geez everybody, calm down. There is an essential question about the bodily handicaps in the story, which gives it some heft ... what is one willing to give away to get cured of a disease thats essentially a living death? Disgust for drinking blood? Cool.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Morbius comes across as a dull exercise in how not to maintain property rights or entertain an audience.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: Humorless and as flat and as uninspired as the Venom movies were, this by-the-numbers comic book action movie seems to be operating entirely on auto-pilot, ticking off plot boxes as it goes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Morbius’s greater fault is that it cleaves away the vampire mythology without replacing that mythology with anything fun, new, or particularly interesting.
reviews.author: Alex Abad-Santos

reviews.text: Morbius is a forgettable, often laughable, entry in Sony’s attempt to fill its own Spider-Man-adjacent cinematic universe, a poorly edited, derivative time suck -- pun intended.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: The film’s plot is lackluster, and there’s no humor, no charm, and no warmth to be found. It’s rare to see a film so devoid of style and ambition, that slugs along like a direct-to-video Underworld sequel.
reviews.author: Chelsea Steiner

reviews.text: Morbius joins the glaring disappointments of Suicide Squad and the yakuza drama The Outsider as the latest instalment in a hit-and-miss career.
reviews.author: Daniel Baksi

reviews.text: It would seem fairly difficult to make a boring vampire flick, let alone one tied to the Marvel universe, but here we have it. Yes, vampires suck, but so does this movie.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Hardly the best in the superhero game, but a decently entertaining and moody entry that's hands down better than the lackluster "Venom" series.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Sucks the fun out of everything.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Morbius has no reason to exist as an actual movie, but maybe that’s why it worked for me.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: An all-around ill-conceived effort sporting a boring hero, an uninteresting villain, and probably the least-appealing visual style of any film this year.
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A nonsensical FrankensteinDraculaJekyll & Hyde mashup from Marvel.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Alas, "Morbius" is too bound to comic book movie convention to become the overt gay vampire superhero melodrama it probably should have been.
reviews.author: Caroline Siede

reviews.text: Morbius had every opportunity to be just as groundbreaking as that other Marvel vampire film was years ago, but instead it feels like just another nail in the coffin of Sonys Spider-verse.
reviews.author: Rick Marshall

reviews.text: Leto tries to turn the biochemist-turned-vampire into a a character of Shakespearean proportion, but is tripped up by the weak, derivative screenplay.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Morbius is a throwback to a simpler and less sophisticated era of superhero movies. Its not terrible, great, or even so bad, its goodits just super average.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Morbius tries to drain the life out of you by boring you to death. It doesn't even do us the courtesy of being so bad it's good.
reviews.author: Dana Han-Klein

reviews.text: Takes the earnest approach to its tale of a brilliant scientist making a grave error of judgment, and then presents it as a slog fraught with clichéd tropes.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: It is so consistently uninventive  even apathetic  that one cannot help but ask if anyone involved even considered the possibility that making a good movie was an option.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: It’s been far too long since I’ve seen a superhero movie whose special effects were both jaw-dropping and seemingly effortless.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: ...when Jared Leto is the best part of your movie, you know you are in serious trouble.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: The film wants the true conflict to be between Morbius and his vampire self. Will Morbius give in to his dark side?...Let me say this again: I. Do. Not. CARE.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: Jared Leto goes the extra mile to bring a minor-league villain from Marvel Comics to the big screen, but this botched horrorfest about the so-called living vampire is less deserving of a sequel than a stake through its heart.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Too many films like Morbius could hasten the death of superhero cinema.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The cast cannot elevate a bland, lifeless narrative with direction from Daniel Espinosa that fails to capture any of the romantic yearning and melancholy associated with vampires or the excitement of the superhero genre the world has grown to love.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: As disappointing as the movie may be, its post-credit sequence is even worse.
reviews.author: Phil Villarreal

reviews.text: Are we sure this isnt some kind of elaborate April Fools Day prank?
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Even at 104 minutes, practically a short by superhero-movie standards, “Morbius” feels draggy.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Despite solid performances and flashes of promise, Morbius is a flat, forgettable affair, failing to deliver an anti-hero origin story we can really sink our teeth into.
reviews.author: Sophie Butcher

reviews.text: It has a truncated, cut-down feel to it, a suspicion supported by the presence of scenes in the trailer that didn't show up in the finished film.
reviews.author: M.V. Moorhead

reviews.text: "Morbius wasnt good: to begin with. There is no doubt whatever about that."
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Morbius's greatest legacy might be that it united the internet to dunk on a movie nobody asked for.
reviews.author: Miles Surrey

reviews.text: Merely adequate, and by Marvel standards, slightly anemic.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: The action sequences are forgettable, a blur of CGI punches and jumping sequences in which Morbius leaves a trail of streamy ribbons in his wake that are supposed to show his flight but instead look like the remnants of a retired cheerleaders pom-pom.
reviews.author: Jo Berry

reviews.text: It's impressive to live in a day and age where comic movies can still be this bad.
reviews.author: Lee McCoy

reviews.text: Morbius isn't a bad movie. It also isn't a particularly memorable one.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: When you combine bad dialogue, questionable editing, and a dead-serious tone - the result is not exactly great.
reviews.author: Marianna Neal

reviews.text: I may not have been a big fan of the Venom films, but it is easy to see their appeal. Hardy is putting his all into an off-the-wall dual performance...With that in mind, I would be hard-pressed to understand what Morbius has to offer.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: It is almost a shame that Morbius is tied to the Marvel universe at all, given that the inclusion brings with it franchise expectations that don't serve the characters key traits at all.
reviews.author: Simon Foster

reviews.text: The script and direction is so bland that even Jared Leto couldn't inject any charm, menace or a skerrick of personality into the character.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Boring! And thats a death knell for anything coming out of Marvel Comic Universe.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Other than being predictable with repetitive visual effects, I found MORBIUS intriguing.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: Morbius delivers a toothless and aggressively soulless descent into beige superhero formula.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Its watchable, but the by-the-numbers execution leaves Morbius just a bit anemic.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: "Morbius" caps off bad month for bat men, but at least it's weird enough to be occasionally enjoyable.
reviews.author: Evan Dossey

reviews.text: Morbius is like a can of flat soda.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: There's a decided B-movie feel hanging over the whole thing, no matter how much gratuitous CGI it throws at us. Simply put, this is not the preferred comics-based bat man to see on screens right now.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: A living vampire and a lifeless movie.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Morbius is a character whos caught between two worlds (man and monster), and his movie is stuck in a similar liminal space that ultimately makes it unremarkable.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: [A] lazy actioner so forced and derivative that it feels like it came out in 2002 rather than 2022.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: Even by the standards of the many monotonous origin stories that have been rolled out during this superhero boom, Daniel Espinosa’s film is a whiff.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: If Instagram had a “blockbuster” filter, this film would use it the whole time.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: Not the best written, but Jared Leto's surprisingly restrained performance mixed with Matt Smith's scenery chewing makes this a decent enough monster movie.
reviews.author: Doug Walker

reviews.text: Morbius is disjointed, rushed, poorly edited, and then it ends abruptly with viewers just kind of staring at their screen wondering what just happened.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Over the years, there have been plenty of mediocre movies associated with the Marvel brand, but I can’t recall one so blatantly willing to leave viewers shortchanged.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: This movie is also devoid of depth. It is emblematic of a system that places amusement park wonderment above sturdy storytelling.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: It starts well, builds to some promise, but ends incredibly clumsily, wasting the likes of Jared Harris (super underrated), Adria Arjona (who has excelled on shows like Good Omens), and yes, believe it or not, even Tyrese. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Not good. It includes a weak story, stale performances, and jerky action and editing. Serves as a reminder of what a disappointing superherocomic film looks like. Full review in Spanish
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: It's as disorienting as a Moebius strip--the effects erase the characters and nearly the entire picture, the script does not care to explain characters or plots, and all we are left with is yet another Spider-Man villain who in reality is a nice guy
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: Jared Leto stars as a sulking, skulking vampire in a bloodless and boring comics adaptation desperately riding the coat-tails of the Marvel movie powerhouse.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: It's ultimately easier to think of Morbius as a campy, marginally entertaining one-off rather than the franchise-starter it so obviously tries to be.
reviews.author: Hayden Mears

reviews.text: Morbius hits the ground running, but the Living Vampire movie is ultimately an uneven film that never quite figures out what it wants to be.
reviews.author: Sam Stone

reviews.text: Unless your ticket is free, don’t bother. This movie is as lifeless as the bodies Morbius drains and throws on the floor.
reviews.author: Emily Zemler

reviews.text: Apparently, the early 2000 days of insultingly lazy superhero movies have not yet died out
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Morbius is a good-enough introduction for a character who most viewers may not know well. Its not spectacular entertainment like the Spider-Man movies, but neither will it have viewers wishing for their money back.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: While most of it is as predictably familiar as expected, it does something unusual for a movie like this: It entertains you, rather than bludgeons you into submission.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: The film is just another vampire movie rather than an origins Marvel story. With a predictable plot, inconsistent beats, flat dialogue and bland characters, Morbius is a huge letdown. The post credits feel like a sloppy afterthought.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: I know that the fans will spend their time and money to see the latest Spidey-verse version entry and more power to them. But, for everyone else without that fandom fervor, why bother?
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Significantly better than Venom but still somewhat lacking in bite, this origin story perhaps inevitably grows more pallid toward the end but until then proves just tasty enough to merit the giving it a shot.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: There's nothing in "Morbius" that couldn't have been better summed up in a two-minute trailer.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: I'm not gonna lie, it's difficult to watch the Joker and the Eleventh Doctor battle it out on-screen with teeth and claws, but Morbius manages to make it work.  It's not a movie everyone will love, but don't dismiss it just yet
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: You can only imagine the carnage that must have taken place in the edit suite.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Soulless, tedious filmmaking. The doldrums of superhero theatrics.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: What could've been an attempt at outright horror succumbs to the usual super-hero sturm und drang, just superpowered characters filling a third act fighting and destroying buildings. In the SonyMarvel universe, even vampires must go big or go home.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: It doesnt even have the so-bad-its-good qualities that made Venom morbidly enjoyable, quickly placing it amongst the worst recent examples of the genre alongside X-Men: Dark Phoenix and 2015s Fantastic Four.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: More like Bore-bius, amirite? The action scenes are poorly staged and the special effects are awful. Plus, it spends much too much time on the origin story somehow without ever making us connect to the title character.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: Morbius is a perfunctory, sloppy, paint-by-numbers attempt to remind audiences that Sony has the rights to these Spider-Man villains and by golly theyre going to use them.
reviews.author: Kyle Anderson

reviews.text: While the latest Marvel origin story features plenty of bats, it doesnt hold a candle to The Batman.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: A dark adventure that gets darker as it goes.
reviews.author: Peter Martin

reviews.text: This might sound silly, but Morbius the Vampire feels like he deserves better.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: There’s little spark in Leto’s performance.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: No harm to Leto, who wears less makeup as a vampire here than he did as a human in House of Gucci, but he appears to be taking the silly role absurdly seriously.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: He's simply not particularly interesting, and neither is his origin story.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Morbius is a fellow tortured by a self-inflicted curse, but his anguish is nothing compared to the pain this terrible movie inflicts on the audience.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: 'Morbius' is a huge step backwards for Sony's Spider-Man Universe, and the worst Marvel-branded movie to come along in a long time.
reviews.author: Scott Campbell

reviews.text: Morbius is what happens when a studio applies a horror filter to an average comic book picture. The filter may shade the original image differently, but its an unconvincing effect.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: At one point Morbius warns, "I'm getting hungry. You wouldn't like me when I'm hungry." My good doctor, we don't like you now! And nothing that occurs before the credits roll changes that.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: It's one of those films like 'Jonah Hex' or 'The Phantom,' something pop culture will occasionally reference in ten or 20 years and we'll all think 'Oh, that's right. They made a movie out of that!'
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: The studio may have accidentally created the first Shepard film: it goes on for about an hour and 45 minutes, and right up until the second it ends, you keep feeling as if it’s just about to start.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A cash-grab so sloppy it makes you wonder if the top brass at Sony are nihilistic members of the undead.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Morbius may be a living vampire, but this supervillain origin story is dead on arrival. A rote, lifeless and cynical attempt to expand Sony’s Spidey-Verse.
reviews.author: Jordan Farley

reviews.text: Lacking in style, spirit, scares, and suspense, this would-be thriller is a toothless and tedious chore.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: 'Morbius' really does... sigh suck. Yes, we couldn't even come up with something more inventive, folks.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: Dull, messy and badly executed, Morbius falls spectacularly short in terms of excitement or entertainment.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: Likely undone by a PG-13 rating that must have shaved off some of, what could have been, effective horror elements, its a defanged vampire movie with no bite.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Watch out for the thrilling moments, gravity-defying stunts and special effects that compensate for what’s missing in making it the action-adventure extravaganza it was expected to be.
reviews.author: Ronak Kotecha

reviews.text: In downplaying Donna’s own extensive work as an activist and the history she is a part of, Bedwani offers up a lacking portrait of her.
reviews.author: Cathy Brennan

reviews.text: It is a muddy puddle of a blockbuster; aimless, dull and lacking in a pulse.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: This is just a total embarrassment to the legacy of Marvel Comics and goes to prove after Spider-Man: No Way Home that Sony really can’t make a good comic book movie without Disney anymore.
reviews.author: George Simpson

reviews.text: My bafflement regarding Leto is becoming chronic, and I’m still recovering from his opera buffa turn and Chico Marx dialect in “House of Gucci.”
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: This is a movie that feels like one big windup for something else, even if we walk out feeling we’ve already seen plenty.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: For a darker, vampiric twist on the superhero origin, Morbius is all bark & no bite  resulting in a formulaic origins tale which descends into a CGI mess.
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: A stylish, special effects-clad vampire flick that'll keep you perfectly entertained on a red eye flight
reviews.author: Caffeinated Clint

reviews.text: Even the action scenes are rendered as pig-ugly blotches of dull pixels, with the climactic scuffle so colourless as to be entirely incomprehensible.
reviews.author: Tom Beasley

reviews.text: Even though there are flashes of promise, Morbius ends up being a bland and confused origin tale of the type we thought we had left behind.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

reviews.text: A fairly good, if gloom-laden jaunt, happily uncluttered by the tangle of poorly told sub-plots that afflict most superhero films...Jared Leto lending just enough serious-actor gravitas to his lines about feeling alive for the first time in his life.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: To call Morbius compelling would be overstating it. But there's enough energy and competent filmmaking here, plus an anchoring performance from Jared Leto, to probably qualify it as worthwhile for many who would be predisposed to care about its existence.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: Morbius has serviceable action but zero surprises.  The film's talented lead actors go through the motions of a rote and predictable anti-hero blockbuster.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: A throwback to the mid-2000s comic book film in all the worst ways. For audiences too young to remember what a lot of comic movies were like before the MCU - here it is, kids! This is what we had to grow up with!
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Morbius sends Marvel back to the bad old pre-Marvel Cinematic Universe days. The characters are poorly drawn, motivations are muddled and special effects are slathered over the film to cover up the patchier elements.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The complexity of the character appears to be there for the writers, but Sazama and Sharpless peel away many potentially interesting problems.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: A monster movie with a little bite, "Morbius" is elevated by some spirited performances and director Daniel Espinosa's sure hand with familiar comic-book material.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: It's a snack in a world of 150+ minute superhero banquets; by the time you notice the meal is lacking a certain something, youre already out the door
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: Featuring scattered storytelling and an unfocused script, Morbius is a huge missed opportunity. Leto is compelling, and his relationship with Smiths Milo had potential, but the movie struggles to bring it all together.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: A flat, dull mess of a blockbuster that commits the cardinal cinematic sin of being unfathomably boring.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: The latest anti-hero saga deserves better than this meandering origin story.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Daniel Espinosas direction is largely pedestrian. Hes more like a work for hire rather than a visionary filmmaker with a distinct visual style.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The best thing about Morbius is it keeps the utterly obvious plot moving along, and isnt exactly boring. But thats hardly a ringing endorsement.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Whatever, man - I liked it! A very good vampire movie starring Jared Leto and Matt Smith, both in top form. Similar to 2009's Daybreakers. As good a launch as 2018's Venom. Fun theater experience if you're into comic book movies.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Its actually a pretty decent premise for a superhero movie, and in its early moments Morbius is quite promising.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Running at 104 minutes, I was pretty impressed by its core theme: health is a privilege.
reviews.author: Diandra Reviews

reviews.text: Morbius works better as a horror movie than as a vampire superhero origin story that's supposed to have a place in the Spider-Man franchise. Morbius has too many plot holes and not enough personality for it to ever be considered a classic superhero film.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Spoiler alert: it's leading to nothing but confusion, as not even Sony knows what they're doing with it. The best possibility here is for none of us to ever find out what would happen next, because, frankly, who cares?
reviews.author: Spencer Perry

reviews.text: If there is any justice in Hollywood, Morbius will be retconned to the margins of superhero cinema history. If the film doesn’t bury the genre alive first, that is.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of Murphy’s Law is demonstrated by this appalling superhero snooze-fest. It’s a movie without dramatic jeopardy, originality, narrative coherence, compelling characters or a single even vaguely human performance.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Morbius does eventually become a cluttered slugfest, as all things must. But for much of its run it is a stylish, intriguingly toned story of a man trying to thwart mortality.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: A misbegotten superhero/horror hybrid.
reviews.author: Katie Rife

reviews.text: Suffering from the same problems of trying to be dark and violent but still all-ages that Venom did, Morbius lacks the staying power and charm of its predecessor due in large part to its lead.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: A bland, competent, and safe superhero adventure that seems destined to be forgotten before its end credits finish rolling.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: Without, say, someone like Tom Hardy embracing the weirdness of the character in Venom, it’s tough to find rooting interest or muster any excitement for the vampiric bat man.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: If superhero movies really are going to dominate modern cinema for the next decade or so, we should at least be allowed a little healthy competition between studios. I hope, in the future, Sony can put up a better fight than this.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Morbius is surprisingly an okay film with Jared Leto delivering a somber performance as the vampiric antihero.
reviews.author: John Nguyen

reviews.text: When you watch Morbius, there's an inescapable sense that someone had to be actively trying to make a movie this bad.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: Mostly, the film occupies a strange no-mans-land of the sprawling Spider-Verse, not charming like the Spider-Man films, not funny like the Venom films, and certainly not technically impressive like the animated “Into the Spider-Verse.”
reviews.author: Kate Erbland

reviews.text: The entire movie, directed by Daniel Espinosa from a script by Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless, is generic -- naggingly, almost jarringly so. You watch it and think, “This is what now passes for a new Marvel chapter?”
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: Is Morbius the worst Marvel movie ever made? In an alternate universe without The New Mutants, the answer would likely be yes.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: Missing much of its connective tissue to make sense of its shenanigans, this titular anti-hero is given a vehicle that takes its foot off the gas not far enough into the ride.
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: This movie isn’t terrible. Leto is good, the VFX work is slick, and there’s modest entertainment to be had here and there. But it seems unlikely to please crowds like Spider-Man: No Way Home.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Morbius is bad, yes, but its not even fun-bad, like the Venom movies; its just kind of depressing.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Morbius is unspectacular in ways that waste the potential of what could be an intriguing hybrid of sinister horror and superhero thrills.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Morbius is a movie Sony has been trying to make since the early 2000s, and the film being released in 2022 feels like a relic from that early 2000s era of superhero movies, and not in a good way.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Morbius, despite the best efforts of its cast, suffers from a number of problems. It’s not a Marvel film showing its A-game. At its absolute best, it’s pedestrian and lacks scope. At its worst, it is unintentionally silly.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: A second-tier MCU movie with some interesting performances and a few flashes of inspiration that unfortunately never goes deeper than superficial storytelling and grows increasingly tiresome over the relatively brief running time.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: The viewer struggles to care. We’re also aware that there are many, many better vampire stories than Count Dreckula here
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: The Marvel superhero-vampire Morbius is with us. And sadly his superpower is being bafflingly dull.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: Writers Matt Sazama and Burk Sharpless don't seem particularly interested in the metaphor of mega-rich Milo seeing the rest of humanity as fuel for his sustenance, but then they don't seem much interested in anything beyond the usual world-building.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: Despite a fine performance from Jared Leto, Morbius is a painfully mediocre superhero origin story, delivering a shallow recreation of better movies.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: Its one of those movies where when it ends you go, 'Oh, thats it? I guess you just decided its time to end there.'
reviews.author: Eric Goldman

reviews.text: Morbius is like a roller coaster without a pulse. There are highs, there are lows, there's plenty of disorientation, and by the end, you aren't upset with the ride, but largely underwhelmed because you have the sense it should have been better.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Rather than a fang-tastic time, Morbius is just a soul-sucking effort.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Morbius is Marvel's most flavorless installment yet...severely lacks energy and excitement, which shows in the final product.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: A modestly scaled launch for the character that succeeds thanks to Leto's performance.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Morbius fails to justify its own existence.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Leto certainly broods up a storm behind his veil of rock-star hair, but the movie has too little to distinguish it from the second-tier Marvel pack, ending up as more of the same
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: There's some kind of invisible force here, hurrying things along in the hopes of a future team-up, making sure Morbius arrives more undead than alive.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Logic and plot flow are generally treated like civilian casualties, but the movie, with its canny mix of whiz-bang violence, goth atmosphere, and high camp, feels pleasingly pulpy and urgent up until its last minutes.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: Morbius has such an anonymous feel to it that it's impossible to work up any strong feelings, one way or another.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Morbius director Daniel Espinosa goes in the other direction. If it’s something you’ve seen before, like a rooftop battle, he’ll give you just enough and no more. But if it’s something new, something interesting between the characters, he lavishes time.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: There is no fun to be had here; there isn't any ironic or so bad its good enjoyment. It's soulless. It's oozing, tar-like gunk that has been spit out of the Hollywood machine, and you should avoid stepping in it.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Morbius is a film that requires one to play along and enjoy the project for what it is. While one absolutely could sit shaking their head as the film plays, it feels entirely possible to get onto the same wavelength as the project and enjoy the ride.
reviews.author: Carson Timar

reviews.text: This might have been a terrific movie if it was still 2005, but no one has asked for this kind of throwback to when comic book movies were just so mediocre and forgettable.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Jared Leto's transformation makes for compelling viewing, but the Living Vampire cant elevate a disappointing story that serves as a powerful, dare we say terrifying, reminder Spider-Man is better off (and safer) in the MCU with Marvel Studios.
reviews.author: Josh Wilding

reviews.text: This thing will suck the energy out of audiences faster than Morbius can drain a vial of artificial blood.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Morbius is a mostly unlikeable mess. The lowest bar any superhero movie has to clear, is that it should at least be fun to watch. Morbius falls at the first hurdle.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: One of the worst popcorn blockbuster experiences in recent memory.
reviews.author: Liam Maguren

synopsis: One of the most compelling and conflicted characters in Sony Pictures Universe of Marvel Characters comes to the big screen as Oscar® winner Jared Leto transforms into the enigmatic antihero Michael Morbius. Dangerously ill with a rare blood disorder and determined to save others suffering his same fate, Dr. Morbius attempts a desperate gamble. While at first it seems to be a radical success, a darkness inside him is unleashed. Will good override evil -- or will Morbius succumb to his mysterious new urges?
